answers.answer: Each player shuffles their chosen hero’s 30 action cards into a separate face-down deck and draws 5. Set hero and sidekick health to their starting values: Alice 13 and Jabberwock 8; Arthur 18 and Merlin 7; Medusa 16 and three Harpies at 1 each; Sinbad 15 and Porter 6. The younger player places their hero on starting space 1, then places each sidekick in a separate space sharing a zone with that hero; if the hero’s space belongs to several zones, any of them may be used. Choose/display Alice’s BIG or SMALL size when placing her (a beginning-of-game choice). Then the older player places their hero on space 2 and sidekicks under the same rules. The younger player takes the first turn.
answers.evidence: Setup: each 30-card deck, draw 5; younger space 1, then sidekicks in separate spaces sharing a zone (any zone of a multizone hero space); older space 2; younger first. Alice size is chosen when placing her. Fighter reference lists starting health.

answers.answer: Take 2 actions from maneuver, scheme, and attack. You may repeat an action, but cannot skip either action. You may hold more than 7 cards during your turn; at its end, discard down to 7. If you have 9 then, discard 2 cards to your own face-up discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: take 2 actions; may repeat, cannot skip; “At the end of your turn” discard excess to your own discard pile until 7.

answers.answer: A maneuver draws 1 card first, mandatorily, then you may move each of your fighters, one at a time, up to that player’s move value (plus applicable bonuses); each may move zero. You may pass through your own fighters, but cannot finish on any occupied space and cannot pass through opposing fighters. Finish one fighter’s movement before starting another’s, so their movements cannot be interleaved.
answers.evidence: Maneuver: draw 1 first; each fighter may move up to move value, including zero; pass through own friendly fighters but not opposing ones; cannot finish occupied; finish one fighter before another.

answers.answer: During a maneuver, discard 1 hand card to add its printed BOOST value (the circled number, not combat value) to that maneuver’s movement value. Every one of your fighters receives the increased allowance. Ignore the discarded card’s effects. A card that cannot be played because its fighter is defeated can still be discarded to BOOST, so a defeated sidekick’s unusable card may pay.
answers.evidence: Maneuver—BOOST movement: discard 1 card to add its BOOST value; each of your fighters receives the allowance; ignore discarded card effects; an unplayable card for a defeated fighter can still be discarded to BOOST.

answers.answer: Do not reshuffle and cannot decline mandatory draws. With an empty deck, each missing card draw causes each of your fighters to take 2 damage. A mandatory draw of 2 therefore causes two separate 2-damage events to every surviving fighter: 4 damage total to each if the duel has not ended. If the hero is defeated during an event, the game ends immediately and later events do not resolve.
answers.evidence: Empty deck: no reshuffle; each required unavailable draw causes each fighter 2 damage. A mandatory draw of 2 causes two separate 2-damage events unless hero defeat already ended the game.

answers.answer: Any fighter may attack an adjacent opponent, even across a zone boundary. A melee fighter cannot attack a nonadjacent target, even if they share a zone. A ranged fighter may attack any opponent sharing its zone regardless of distance or adjacency; this includes a disconnected part of the same colored zone.
answers.evidence: Attack declaration: any fighter may attack adjacent opponents across zones; melee only adjacent; ranged also any opponent sharing a zone regardless of distance, including separated parts of that zone.

answers.answer: An attack action is illegal if you lack an attack-capable card or none of your fighters has a valid target. Declare the attacking fighter and target. The attacker plays a face-down attack card that fighter may use; the defender may decline a card or play a legal defense card for the defending fighter. Reveal simultaneously after both choices. Versatile cards may attack or defend and count as both attack and defense cards for other effects. Fighter-specific cards are restricted to that fighter; ANY may be used by any of your fighters.
answers.evidence: Attack: cannot act without an attack-capable card or valid target; declare attacker/target; legal attack and defense cards face down; defender may decline; reveal simultaneously. Versatile counts as both attack and defense for other effects.

answers.answer: Resolve combat in this order: (1) IMMEDIATELY card effects; (2) DURING COMBAT effects; (3) attack damage minus defense (minimum zero), then reduce defender health; (4) AFTER COMBAT card effects; (5) other after-combat game effects such as a hero ability; (6) put played cards in their owners’ discard piles. When effects share a timing, defender resolves first. Card effects are mandatory unless they say otherwise, and printed order is followed.
answers.evidence: Combat timing, damage and winning combat gives the ordered six phases; “Whenever effects share a timing, the defender’s effect resolves first”; card effects are mandatory unless otherwise stated; played cards go to respective discard piles.

answers.answer: The attack deals 0 damage because 4 minus 4 is 0, so the defender wins combat; the later 2 damage from a card effect does not change the combat winner. With no defense card, an attack value of 4 deals 4 damage.
answers.evidence: Combat damage is attack minus defense, minimum zero; winning combat requires the attack itself to deal at least 1 damage, and effect damage does not change the winner. No defense card means take attack value.

answers.answer: Remove a defeated sidekick token immediately. Its played card’s after-combat effect still resolves unless the game has already ended. If a hero reaches zero, that hero immediately loses and the game ends; do not continue pending effects to heal the hero or finish the turn.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: immediately remove defeated sidekick; defeated hero ends game at once, do not continue pending effects. Combat timing says defeated fighter’s played card still resolves unless game already ended.

answers.answer: Play a scheme face up from hand, declaring an eligible active fighter according to its fighter label; you cannot play it if its listed fighter is defeated. Resolve its effect, then put it in your discard pile. Both players may inspect either player’s face-up discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Scheme: play face up, declare fighter allowed by label, cannot play if listed fighter defeated, resolve and discard. Cards section: both players may inspect either discard pile at any time.

answers.answer: Alice starts at 13 health, is melee, and has move 2. Jabberwock starts at 8 health and is melee. Choose Alice’s BIG or SMALL size when placing her at setup. BIG adds 2 to Alice’s attack-card values; SMALL adds 1 to Alice’s defense-card values, including versatile cards used in that role. These bonuses belong to Alice, not Jabberwock.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference lists Alice 13/melee/2 and Jabberwock 8/melee. Alice ability states setup size choice and BIG +2 attack / SMALL +1 defense; bonuses belong to Alice, not Jabberwock.

answers.answer: Arthur starts at 18 health, is melee, and has move 2; Merlin starts at 7 health, is ranged, and shares the player’s move value 2. When Arthur attacks, he may play a hand card face down alongside his attack card and add its BOOST value, ignoring its effects; discard that BOOST card. If the opponent cancels the effects on Arthur’s attack card, the ability’s BOOST is discarded without effect.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference lists Arthur 18/melee/2 and Merlin 7/ranged; maneuver value applies to each fighter. Arthur ability says when he attacks he may BOOST with a face-down card and that a canceled attack card’s effects nullify this BOOST.

answers.answer: Medusa starts at 16 health, has move 3, and is ranged. She has 3 Harpies, each with 1 health and melee attack. At the start of Medusa’s turn, she may (optionally) deal 1 damage to one opposing fighter in Medusa’s zone. It is not an attack action and does not require adjacency; Harpies do not project this ability from their own zones.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference gives Medusa and Harpy stats. Medusa ability specifies start of turn, optional 1 damage to an opposing fighter in Medusa’s zone, no adjacency requirement; Harpies do not project it.

answers.answer: Sinbad starts at 15 health, is melee, and has normal move 2. Porter starts at 6 health, is melee, and shares move value 2. With 3 Voyages already in the discard pile, each fighter may move up to 2 + 3 = 5 spaces in a maneuver, before any maneuver BOOST. A newly played base-2 Voyage has combat value 2 + 3 = 5. The played Voyage does not count itself.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference gives Sinbad/Porter health and attack types; move applies to each fighter. Sinbad ability gives +1 move per Voyage in discard and +1 Voyage attack value per other Voyage in discard; currently played card is not yet there.

answers.answer: Eat Me is a scheme: move Alice up to 3 spaces, then change size. Drink Me is a scheme: draw 2 cards, then change size. Those effects are mandatory: she cannot refuse the size change after the first benefit (unless an effect is explicitly optional, which these are not).
answers.evidence: Alice card reference lists Eat Me: move up to 3, then change size; Drink Me: draw 2, then change size. General card rule says effects are mandatory unless they say otherwise.

answers.answer: The attack deals 0 damage (4 minus 4), so Arthur wins combat because the attack itself dealt no damage. Same-timing defender effects resolve first: Arthur’s Skirmish may move Jabberwock up to 2 spaces; in the stated setup it moves Jabberwock so it has no adjacent fighter. Jaws That Bite then finds no adjacent fighter and deals no damage. If a friendly fighter alone were adjacent, Jaws must deal 2 damage to it; Alice cannot decline that mandatory effect.
answers.evidence: Combat winner requires attack damage; same timing defender first; Skirmish moves a fighter in combat if its player won. The summary’s timing example explicitly says Skirmish can move Jabberwock before Jaws checks adjacency; Jaws damages any one adjacent fighter, including a friendly one, and is mandatory.

answers.answer: At 4 health, Arthur is not defeated and the Holy Grail sets him to 8. At 5 health, nothing happens because he has more than 4. At 0 health, he is defeated and the duel has already ended, so the Grail does not resolve to heal him. Recovery cannot raise any fighter above the maximum on that fighter’s dial; for Arthur the stated dial maximum is his starting 18.
answers.evidence: Holy Grail: if Arthur has 4 or less health but is not defeated, set health to 8; at 5+ nothing; at 0 duel already ended. Recovery cannot exceed dial maximum; Arthur dial starts at 18.

answers.answer: Winged Frenzy lets each of Medusa’s fighters move up to 3 spaces and pass through opposing fighters. Afterward, if there is a defeated Harpy, return one such Harpy to any unoccupied space in Medusa’s zone. It cannot end on an occupied space.
answers.evidence: Winged Frenzy: move each of your fighters up to 3, they may pass through opposing fighters; then return a defeated Harpy, if any, to any unoccupied space in Medusa’s zone. General place rule retains one fighter per space.

answers.answer: The Voyage’s combat value is 2 + 4 = 6, since each of the four other Voyages in the discard pile adds 1; the newly played Voyage does not count itself. After combat, Voyage Home takes all other Voyage cards from the discard pile into Sinbad’s hand. Voyage Home itself then goes to the discard pile at the normal end of combat. With those four others removed and Home as the sole Voyage remaining in the discard pile, Sinbad’s next unboosted maneuver allowance is 2 + 1 = 3 spaces for each of his fighters.
answers.evidence: Voyages are A/2 and gain +1 per other Voyage in discard during combat; current played card is not yet in pile. Voyage Home returns all other Voyages from discard to hand, then Home goes to discard at normal combat end. Maneuver bonus is +1 per Voyage in discard, applied to each fighter’s normal move 2.
